summary:
I've been heads-down on **BudgetTracker** for the past several weeks. The biggest milestone was migrating the whole database off MSSQL onto PostgreSQL on Supabase, including a full Drizzle ORM rewrite — no compatibility shim, since it was a good window for breaking changes while the user count was still just me. After that landed, I built out a complete MCP tool surface (11 read-only tools) that lets my Hermes home agent query things like upcoming obligations, cash-flow projections, and spending anomalies. The interesting constraint there was keeping the math in SQL — the agent reasons over deterministic outputs, never runs arithmetic itself.

A few things followed from that foundation. I wired up a Hermes→BudgetTracker webhook channel so that after a bank sync, the agent wakes up, pulls the computed figures, and sends a proportional summary to my phone. That involved tracing a 401 bug down to a signature-scheme mismatch: BudgetTracker signs Stripe-style (timestamp + body), Hermes validates body-only, and fixing it meant sending both headers. I also ran a security audit: the notable finding was a path traversal in the receipt image endpoint (`..%2f` escaped the upload directory) plus upload magic-byte spoofing. The SSRF guard for user-supplied LLM endpoints landed with an intentional operator-vs-user boundary — operator-configured endpoints can be private, user-supplied ones must be public HTTPS, so a self-hosted deployment can't be used as a relay into internal infrastructure.

On a smaller scale, I built **Cadence** — an RSVP speed-reader that mirrors Claude Code's live transcript and flashes replies one word at a time with adaptive pacing. The pacing overlay comes from a Haiku scorer that returns density weights keyed to word indices; the engine applies them as clamped dwell multipliers without rewriting the text. There's a web GUI with a session picker, the speed-reader itself, and a server-side `/api/score` endpoint so the browser never handles the API credential. I also found and fixed a filemover bug where browsing to a subdestination wasn't committing the transfer target, so files landed in the parent folder instead.

highlights.oneLiner: Security audit (path traversal, magic-byte spoofing, SSRF guard) shipped; 12th MCP tool and latent Postgres bugs fixed
Brain flipped from Gemma to Qwen3.6-35B; toolset trimmed 32K→20K tokens; spending section wired into morning briefing
Daily spending section added to morning briefing, composed by local Qwen to keep financial data off cloud LLMs
BudgetTracker MCP tool surface grew to 12 read-only tools; webhook signature fix unblocked Hermes-triggered financial reviews
